China Tower Corporation Limited (0788.HK) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
sum: China Tower Corporation Limited, together with its subsidiaries, provides telecommunication tower infrastructure services in the People's Republic of China. The company engages in the construction, maintenance, and operation of base station ancillary facilities, such as telecommunications towers and public network coverage in high-speed railway tunnels and subways, large-scale indoor distributed antenna systems, and integrated digital infrastructure service. It also offers towers, and shelters or cabinets; and ancillary equipment to TSPs to facilitate the operating of their telecommunications equipment. In addition, the company provides maintenance services, including monitoring equipment operation, routine inspection, device breakdown handling, property upkeep, working environment protection, and operation analysis services. Further, it offers power access, batteries, or back up power generation to the customers' telecommunications equipment; and indoor distributed antenna systems connecting telecommunication equipment, enabling them to receive and send indoor mobile telecommunication network signals, as well as mobile telecommunication network signals covering large venues, buildings, and tunnels. Additionally, the company provides backup power services for standby emergency power supply to corporate customers; battery exchange services to replaceable batteries to individual customers; battery recharge services to corporate and individual customers; and trans-sector site application and information services, as well as integrated information, power generation, and energy storage services. The company was formerly known as China Communications Facilities Services Corporation Limited and changed its name to China Tower Corporation Limited in September 2014. The company was incorporated in 2014 and is headquartered in Beijing, China.

Nvidia CEO Exit Saga Fuels Rally in Chinese AI Chip Stocks; Domestic Share Seen Near 90% in 2026
sum: On Nov. 12, the AI chip sector on China's A-share market bucked the broader trend. Enflame Technology rose more than 13% intraday, MetaX gained nearly 9%, and Moore Threads and Cambricon each climbed more than 8%, with Intellifusion, Biren Technology (Hong Kong-listed) and Hygon Information Technology following higher. The immediate trigger for the rally was fresh developments in the question of whether Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang will stay or go.

According to the Shanghai Securities News, foreign media cited people familiar with the matter as saying that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove Huang, and could hold a meeting as early as Thursday local time to decide his fate. Huang had previously acknowledged an extramarital affair, prompting the Nvidia board to launch an independent investigation; subsequent reports said he had an affair with Kimberly Powell, the company's vice president of healthcare. Under Nvidia's code of conduct, employees must "avoid situations that create a conflict of interest," including "personal relationships." The report also said Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify potential new CEO candidates and is considering appointing an interim CEO before a broader search.

In response to the rumors, Zhang Guobin, founder and CEO of EET China, laid out three lines of observation in an interview. On the litigation front, a shareholder class action was filed after the close on Nov. 9 against Nvidia and Huang personally, with the core allegations centering on four statements the company made about Megaspeed. It is the second securities class action against Huang, and together with a $5.5 million penalty from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in 2022, the disclosure records of both Huang and the company are being re-examined. On the congressional front, three House committees have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18 on issues including Megaspeed's procurement and chip flows. On the corporate governance front, the board could, under the code of conduct, remove him at the most severe end of the scale, but several Silicon Valley figures judge that he faces no immediate risk of departure — Huang has an enormous influence on Nvidia's operations and share price, and the company has no clear No.

Zhipu Launches HK$4 Billion Share Buyback as Chairman Liu Debing Leads the Charge
sum: Hong Kong-listed Chinese large-model developer Zhipu (02513.HK) announced the launch of an H-share repurchase program with a cap of HK$4 billion (approximately $509.8 million). The news sent the stock gapping higher in early trading on the 11th, surging more than 6% intraday to a high of HK$512.

According to a voluntary announcement Zhipu released on the evening of the 10th, the buyback stems from a share repurchase proposal by Chairman Liu Debing. The company will buy back its own H-shares on the open market at opportune times under the general mandate granted at its annual shareholders' meeting on June 22, 2026. The total repurchase amount is capped at HK$4 billion, with a second threshold: the number of shares bought back may not exceed 1% of the total issued shares as of the announcement date. Both limits must be satisfied simultaneously.

Zhipu said in the announcement that the repurchase plan primarily demonstrates management's confidence in the group's long-term business outlook and prospects, as well as its commitment to enhancing shareholder value. In execution, the board will take into account the company's financial position, working capital needs and business development to ensure sufficient financial resources remain for daily operations and growth. The company also cautioned that this is only a repurchase intention, and the timing, price and actual number of shares bought back will be at the board's discretion based on market conditions, with no guarantee of full execution.

The announcement also stated that the board and authorized persons will not exercise the repurchase mandate in a way that would trigger a mandatory offer obligation under Rule 26 of the Takeovers Code, or reduce the proportion of H-shares held by public shareholders below the minimum threshold required by the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong. The mandate is valid until the conclusion of the company's 2026 annual shareholders' meeting, or the date shareholders revoke or amend the mandate by special resolution, whichever occurs earlier.
Market participants analyzed that the buying wave reflects not only the buyback theme but also expectations of a valuation recovery for the large-model sector.

sum: Nvidia shares fell 4.3 percent in New York on Monday despite a Wall Street rally in tech shares after the chipmaker's board opened an independent inquiry into whether Chief Executive Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Huang, 63, admitted and apologized for an extramarital affair with a Singapore-based businesswoman now suspected of gathering intelligence for China. US President Donald Trump later told a press briefing that the FBI is investigating the affair but Huang has assured him he had had no idea she might be a spy. China's Foreign Ministry dismissed the espionage allegation as a baseless smear.

The fate of Taiwan-born Huang – co-founder of Nvidia 33 years ago, mastermind of its growth into the world's most valuable chip company and a sort of an AI rock star – isn't clear. If he were forced out, there's no clear successor. The company's directors said they have "confidence in Jensen" and "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." Elon Musk and other industry moguls have come out in support of Huang.

The 31st UN Climate Change Conference has begun in Turkey following a year that has produced record high temperatures and increasing natural disasters blamed on a warming planet. Representatives from about 190 countries are debating how to address a climate crisis that shows little signs of slowing. The world's biggest emitter of greenhouse gases won't be attending. The US pulled out of global climate agreements after President Trump took office nearly two years ago and began dismantling pollution control policies. Past summits of the UN group have focused on setting limits on harmful emissions, though implementation has fallen short of goals. The climate debate is complicated by continuing friction between rich and poor countries over who pays for the impact of the climate crisis. Africa, in particular, which has faced prolonged droughts and destructive flooding, says it contributes little to greenhouse gas emissions and should receive funds to cope with the fallout. And low-lying island nations in the Pacific Ocean that are particularly susceptible to rising sea levels want aid.

China Mobile Partners with Zhipu: Chinese-Made Computing Power Fully Integrated with GLM Models
sum: China Mobile (00941.HK) and Zhipu (02513.HK) have formally signed a cooperation agreement, under which the two sides will pursue deep collaboration in three major areas: Chinese-made computing power, Large Language Model services, and the commercialization of artificial intelligence. Zhipu's GLM series models will also be integrated into China Mobile's model service system.

Under the arrangement, the two parties will carry out joint innovation on adaptation of Chinese-made computing power, improvements in Token production efficiency, development of AI Coding products, and industry applications such as finance and government affairs, with the goal of accelerating the large-scale deployment of Large Language Models in key industries. From a technology-chain perspective, the cooperation spans the complete chain from underlying computing power supply and model services to commercial distribution.

Zhipu believes that allying with China Mobile will help connect the upstream and downstream segments of the industrial chain, improve model inference efficiency, and expand the scale of GLM model usage and commercialization channels, driving Large Language Models from independent technological innovation toward large-scale industrial application. Overseas reports noted that the GLM models will be connected to China Mobile's Mobile Cloud model-as-a-service platform, a move that also echoes the direction of China's official AI policy at the current stage, which emphasizes Chinese-made computing power and application deployment.
The market reacted positively to the news, with Zhipu's shares rising more than 5% in early trading to HK$448.4 (approximately NT$1,900).

items.t: Is VNET Group (VNET) Undervalued After Earnings Growth Met Leverage Concerns?
sum: VNET Group (VNET) has drawn fresh attention after its latest quarter showed 14.2% revenue growth and a 133.3% rise in earnings per share, set against a balance sheet carrying net debt of 6.8x EBITDA.

VNET Group’s share price has fallen sharply despite the latest earnings jump, with a 30 day share price return down 41.5% and the year to date share price return down 65.4%. The 5 year total shareholder return has declined 82.4%, pointing to fading momentum and a market that continues to price in balance sheet risk even as revenue growth and large scale data center contracts draw fresh interest.

Spot opportunities with similar pressure points by scanning our hand-picked 39 high quality undervalued stocks. These ideas combine growth stories with compressed valuations and balance sheets that investors are still questioning.

For VNET Group, the gap between growing data center revenue and a shrinking share price raises a simple tension: Is the latest slide signaling deeper business issues, or has sentiment pushed the valuation too far down?

VNET Group last closed at $3.16, while the most followed narrative anchors on a fair value of $12.71. This frames the recent share price slide against a much higher long term expectation based on growth and risk assumptions.

Strong, sustained growth in wholesale data center capacity utilization and demand, especially for AI-driven workloads in regions like Greater Beijing and Yangtze River Delta, positions VNET to benefit from the accelerating digitalization and increased AI/cloud adoption across China, directly supporting higher future revenues and occupancy rates.
Still, the VNET Group story leans heavily on high leverage and large 2025 CapEx plans, so any refinancing hiccup or weaker wholesale demand could quickly reset expectations.

items.t: Ambani’s Jio soars 21% on Mumbai debut
sum: MUMBAI: Shares of billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio Platforms ​soared 21% in their Mumbai debut yesterday, making it India's second-largest company ‌by market capitalisation, valued at about US$131.5 billion (RM537 billion). Jio, whose telecoms ​business serves more than 530 million customers, is backed by Meta Platforms and Alphabet's Google. Its user numbers are second only to China Mobile on the basis of single-country subscribers. The listing, the ​first for the Reliance conglomerate in two decades, furthers Ambani's plan to turn Reliance from an oil-and-chemicals conglomerate ‌into an “everything company” spanning ​consumer products and technology. The listing ceremony was ​attended by Mukesh Ambani, Akash Ambani, his eldest son and Jio's managing ​director, and his wife Nita Ambani. Ambani's other children Isha and Anant Ambani also attended. The stock opened at 1,358 rupees a share, compared with its 1,119-rupee offer price. Jio's market capitalisation overtook Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank, becoming the second-largest Indian firm by that metric. Several brokerages see a potential upside for the Jio stock, but they flagged competition, heavy capital spending and changes in India's telecom rules, including those related to spectrum, licensing and fees. “Jio has had a strong debut even despite geopolitical issues and turbulent market conditions … the revenues and earnings will lead the ‌stock here onwards,“ said Kranthi Bathini, equity strategist at WealthMills Securities. The Ambani family rang the IPO bell on stage at the National Stock Exchange in Mumbai. An emotional Mukesh ​Ambani was seen in tears as Anant traced Reliance's and Jio's legacies and journey in a ​speech ​at the ceremony. Major Indian newspapers yesterday carried front-page ads from Reliance ‌Jio, saying “Thank ​you, India.” India has become the world's busiest IPO market this year in terms of the number of deals, with 246 listings so far, though it ranked fourth by money raised at US$13.5 billion, behind the US, mainland China and ​Hong Kong, LSEG data showed. – Reuters

As I get older, my investment strategy has changed quite a bit.Compared to before, I now try to minimize exposure to high-leverage products. I’m not sharing this to be cynical, but rather to help you avoid common pitfalls through my investment experience. There will always be opportunities in the market, but if you lose too much of your principal, it’s extremely difficult to recover.

China Mobile Stock Technicals: Gains 1.91% on Friday, Testing Key Resistance
sum: On October 30, 2026: price 80.00 HKD, trend sideways, RSI 56.4, support 77.10, resistance 81.00. technical analysis of china mobile stock.

China Mobile’s shares rose 1.91% to HKD 80.00 in Friday’s Hong Kong session, October 30, as trading volume surged and the MACD histogram turned positive. The move is notable because it was about 1.4 times the stock’s average daily trading range, but the broader trend remains sideways and on-balance volume fell, leaving a gap between price strength and underlying buying participation.

That makes China Mobile a useful read on whether a burst of activity can push the shares through nearby resistance—or whether the rally runs into supply. The stock gained 3.76% over five days, while its one-month advance was a more modest 0.69%, according to the supplied market data.

China Mobile ended above its 20-day moving average of HKD 79.14, a short-term positive, but that average remained below the 50-day average of HKD 79.39. The 20-day average fell 0.22% over five days, so the latest price rise has not yet changed the underlying direction of that trend measure. No new moving-average crossover was recorded.

The shares were positioned at 74% of their 20-day trading range, between support at HKD 77.10 and resistance at HKD 81.00. That places price closer to the upper boundary, where a sustained break could signal that buyers are overcoming resistance. The three-month high of HKD 84.95 remains a more distant reference point; the three-month low was HKD 77.00.
As shown in the chart, the shares are above the 20-day average but still face resistance near the top of the recent range.

Momentum indicators leaned mildly constructive without showing an extreme. The RSI was 56.4, in neutral territory; the Relative Strength Index measures the pace of recent price moves, and this reading does not indicate that the stock is stretched in either direction. Stochastic %K at 64.5 stood above %D at 39.8, also within neutral territory, suggesting improving short-term momentum rather than a decisive breakout signal.
